summary: Dedup token mismatch on multipart/stream retry causing duplicate external tool invocation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external webhook/tool invocations when using multipart streaming with client-side exponential backoff. The client sends an initial chunk that triggers a downstream tool call. If the connection is reset shortly after the first chunk, the client retries by re-sending the initial chunk but the downstream tool receives two executions.

Impact:
- Duplicate downstream side-effects (webhook POSTs to third-party billing endpoint) observed for ~2% of streamed requests from AcmeHealth in us-east for the past 36 hours.
- Customer is on Dedicated plan and is seeing billing inaccuracies and duplicated orders in their downstream system.

Environment:
- Customer dedicated pool (dedicated-us-east-2), SDKs: Python v1.14.2 and TS v0.9.6.
- Edge proxy version: edge-proxy v2.8.1 behind an internal gateway appliance.
- Model: redwood-llm-xl (pinned v2026-02-20).

Steps to reproduce (attempted by Support):
1) Use python SDK streaming example to send a multipart request initiating a tool call on first chunk.
2) Simulate a short TCP connection reset right after first chunk (iptables drop / test client network flap).
3) Client retries initial chunk according to exponential backoff (client-side retry).
4) Server processes both chunks as separate requests and forwards to external webhook/tool twice.

Observed logs / evidence provided by customer:
- Redacted request traces show two different ingestion timestamps but identical body and missing second dedup header on retried chunk (see snippet below).
- Downstream webhook logs show two POSTs within ~800ms.

Header snippet from traces:
- First attempt headers: x-rw-idempotency: "txn-7f2b-9a3c", x-rw-stream-id: "s-01b2", content-type: multipart/stream
- Retransmit headers: x-rw-stream-id: "s-01b2", content-type: multipart/stream (x-rw-idempotency header absent)
comments: Priya Rao (Support) - 2026-03-10: Ticket created with customer logs and sample traces. Noted client SDK versions and edge-proxy in front of dedicated pool.
Diego Martinez (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Running a repro in staging with identical SDK and proxy versions. Suspect header being stripped by gateway on retry splice.

Asha Patel (Customer Engineer) - 2026-03-11: Customer confirmed they see duplicate order entries in their system and can reproduce reliably when using local network flaps. They provided full webhook logs and a capture of the client's retry code path.

Diego Martinez (SRE) - 2026-03-11: Found that our ingress path treats retried chunk parts as separate HTTP/1.1 requests; some chunks from the client do not include the x-rw-idempotency header because SDK attaches it only at initial connect. Edge-proxy configuration drops custom headers on request re-origin for certain retry paths.
Priya Rao (Support) - 2026-03-12: Shared interim workaround to customer (see resolution notes). Customer applied workaround and reported immediate reduction in duplicates in canary traffic.
investigation_notes: Reproduced in staging by simulating TCP reset at 300ms after initial chunk; observed two server-side ingestion events without idempotency mapping.
Edge-proxy (v2.8.1) rewrites internal hop and by default strips non-standard headers when generating a new request on retry. Confirmed with tcpdump and proxy debug logs.

SDK behavior: python-sdk v1.14.2 attaches x-rw-idempotency only on initial stream open; subsequent chunks sent on reconnection reuse stream-id but do not reattach header in current SDK implementation.

Serving runtime dedup logic expects x-rw-idempotency or per-action nonce. When header missing, the runtime deduplicates by (stream-id, sequence) only which appears different on the retry path leading to duplicate external calls.
No evidence of model-level re-execution; duplication occurs at call-to-tool stage (function/tool invocation pipeline).
root_cause: Combination of SDK design (idempotency header attached only at stream init) and edge-proxy behavior that strips custom headers on request re-origin during client reconnection, resulting in retried chunks lacking the idempotency token and being treated as fresh tool-invoking requests.
temporary_workaround: Customer guidance: update client to explicitly attach x-rw-idempotency header on every chunk (works around SDK limitation). Example: modify streaming send loop in python to include header if reconnecting.
Enable edge-proxy config flag 'preserve-custom-headers-on-retry=true' if appliance supports it. Customer's gateway vendor provides this toggle; advised to pilot in staging.
On Redwood side, we recommended enabling request-level dedup by using a per-action nonce included in the JSON chunk body (action.nonce) as a fallback dedup key.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12: Engineering accepted a fix: edge-proxy patch to preserve x-rw-idempotency on retry paths (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/412).

2026-03-13: SDK teams agreed to ship a minor release that attaches x-rw-idempotency to every chunk on reconnect: python-sdk v1.14.3 and ts-sdk v0.9.7 (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/189).
2026-03-13: Deployed proxy patch to dedicated-us-east-2 canary with monitoring for duplicate-tool-call metric. Canary showed duplicate rate drop from ~2% to <0.1%.
Follow-up: Add server-side defensive matching to accept an action.nonce in chunk body as alternate dedup key (RFC to be created on Confluence).
next_steps: Ship SDK patch to python/ts and notify customers in release notes with guidance to set per-chunk idempotency where possible.
Roll out edge-proxy patch to remaining dedicated clusters after canary validation (tracking rollout in INT-1876).
Create a short support KB article describing multipart-stream retry pitfalls and recommended patterns for idempotency tokens and per-action nonces.
Add automated test in serving-runtime to simulate retried chunk behavior and assert dedup correctness.
Monitor duplicates metric for AcmeHealth for 72 hours post-rollout and follow up with customer.
